AD-4120.title: UI/UX 47: Airbnb: Batch Calendar Operations: Set limits to the payload.
AD-4120.description:
This was confirmed by Ricardo in Asana, and recently added to the Airbnb documentations.

For the batch calendar operations API: https://developer.airbnb.com/reference/async-calendar-batch-operations set the following limits in our payload based on these documentations:

Calendar validation

Requests that send information for dates beyond 1125 days (3 years and 30 days) from the date of the request will fail with a 400 Validation error. To avoid errors, do not permit hosts to set availability for dates more than 1125 days into the future.

Batch Limits

The number of total dates in one call can be no more than 731 (2 years).

One call can have multiple operations, and each operation can have multiple dates, but the aggregated total number of dates of all operations must be equal to or less than 731.

AD-4129.title: 100 update listing mapping calls from XML > REST
AD-4129.description:
On the listing mapping page (for example: https://boost.rezfusion.com/v2/app/organizations/10/channels/1381/tools/listing-mapping ) when a connection is saved, the API call we make is the POST Create Listing Import. We need to update this to use the POST update listing REST endpoint (https://developer.airbnb.com/v2021.12.31/reference/updatelisting) for any listings that are REST enabled (via rest_api_enabled field in rc_airbnb_listing_data table). This can be accessed by calling $listing->getMetadata()->getRestApiEnabled().

We will probably need to update this method, which gets called when saving the listing mapping page/form:

https://github.com/PropertyBrands/btt-site-d7-api-api.rescmshost.com/blob/master/sites/all/modules/rescms/rc_airbnb/src/API/V2/Repository/ListingRepository.php#L124-L128

If rest_api_enabled is true, I believe we only need to set the listing_id internally in Boost to the rc_channels_listing.remote_id and rc_airbnb_listing_data.listing_id fields. We may not need to make an api call at all. Please try this out and see if it works. It would work if after listing_id is saved, you could then go and do a listing import/sync action from the listings page without any errors.

Also as part of the save process and after the listing_id is saved, we should queue up the REST publications to sync. Should be able to call this method for that - https://github.com/PropertyBrands/btt-site-d7-api-api.rescmshost.com/blob/master/sites/all/modules/rescms/rc_channels/src/Queue/PublicationEnqueuer.php#L42

I believe there is logic on the UI side for the mapping page to check the airbnb listing response data and see if synchronization_category is set or not to know if a listing is already mapped/connected or not. I think synchronization_category is no longer used for REST listing, and the field is only for XML. We will probably need to update the UI logic to not show the unit as “disconnected” if sync_category is null but the listing is REST enabled.

RES-892.title: LiveRez Support for Quotehold
RES-892.description:
[11:45 AM] Sina Floyd Jason Landa we have a partner that is set up to use Quotehold for Vrbo but the reservations are coming back in as approved. Should they come back in as pending?  http://bluepacificvacationrentals.com  | Blue Pacific Vacation Rentals | 12858 Transaction example: 8159393

Jamie: on POST /reservations/channel/booking it looks like we can set status to “approved” or “pending” but we appear to be setting al channel bookings to “approved” today.

Boost has an option to select Booking Policy

There is an option in there for quote hold, can use the example Sina sent for this being set to Quote Hold

https://boost.rezfusion.com/v2/app/organizations/480/channels/663/settings

The booking policy is in the listing configuration published to VRBO.  This is not part of the booking request.  It is returned in the booking response as UNCONFIRMED reservation status.

Booking Request → VrboOrderBuilderBooking::buildOrder() adds quote hold booking policy based on listing config → SPS orderSubmit() → BookingResponseSourceItem::getReservationStatus() returns UNCONFIRMED in booking response

Possible ways to identify these in LDRCOrder.  On the line item makes sense at it is tied to specific listing. But we really only support a single reservation item at this time.

	- With the line item rcav params ['rcav']['booking_policy']

	- Part of the channel params ['channel_source']['booking_policy']

	- $order->engine_custom['booking_policy']

HASP uses bookingType in rcav params

if($params['rcav']['bookingType'] & LDRCBooking::TYPE_OWNER) {

{{  $hts[] = Reservation::HOLD_TYPE_OWNER;}}

For the BUS LDRCBooking::getType() exists with 5 types.  TYPE_HOLD would correspond to a pending or quote hold booking.  BUS will need to use LDRCBooking::isCancelled() along with getType() to determine the status.

UNCONFIRMED
CONFIRMED

CANCELLED_BY_OWNER (not valid in <bookingResponse>)
CANCELLED_BY_TRAVELER (not valid in <bookingResponse>)

const TYPE_DEFAULT = 1;
const TYPE_OWNER = 2;
const TYPE_OWNER_GUEST = 4;
const TYPE_MAINTENANCE = 8;
const TYPE_HOLD = 16;

Coming out of LiveRez the status is described as one of the following:

"APPROVED" "PENDING" "CANCELLED" "DECLINED"

Probably going to be Boost work, then Core work.

New booking, BUS updates, etc.
